scope: Correct the shared generated-frame test helper for R2013+ DWG object handle sizes, then re-enable the AC1027 BLOCK_CONTROL boundary selector.

evidenceBasis.authority: ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 section 20.1: the R2010+ object handle-stream size is measured in bits and includes terminal padding.
evidenceBasis.sourceProfile: The hash-bound AC1027 BLOCK_CONTROL profile has 35 data bits before its handle tokens, 48 token bits, and five terminal padding bits. Its UMC handle-size value is therefore 53, which is not byte-aligned.

diagnosis.failure: The test helper rejected every R2010+ handle-size value whose low three bits were nonzero. That byte-alignment assumption contradicted the source-backed AC1027 BLOCK_CONTROL profile.
diagnosis.instrumentedObservation: The AC1027 writer published BLOCK_CONTROL handle 1 at object-map offset 7644; frame capture reached the generic alignment rejection. No production writer failure was observed.

change.details: Treat the UMC as a bit count, bound it by total object-body bits, and assert the exact AC1027 empty BLOCK_CONTROL frame has an 11-byte body, 53 handle bits, and handle-stream start bit 35.

fixturePolicy: No DWG/DXF fixture was added or committed; validation uses the runtime-generated writer control.
limits: Test-only correction based on the exact source-bound AC1027 control profile. No writer, reader, parser, binary ABI, format-support, interoperability, or consumer claim changed.
